title: Cyanidin-3-glucoside confers neuroprotection in ischemic stroke by targeting NOX4-mediated oxidative stress: A network pharmacology and experimental validation study.
authors: Li, Xiaoting; Gao, Yikun; Ye, Yingze; Wang, Jin; Xiong, Xiaoxing; Zhang, Jiehua; Wei, Liang; Gu, Lijuan
one_liner_zh: 该文研究花青素C-3-G通过靶向NOX4发挥脑缺血保护作用，核心为小分子-蛋白互作与氧化应激通路，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，且无AI/物理模拟方法用于核酸-蛋白体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate the neuroprotective effect of the dietary anthocyanin cyanidin-3-glucoside (C-3-G) in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms by a network pharmacology and transcriptomics methods. METHODS: We employed a network pharmacology and transcriptomics approach to identify NOX4 as a key therapeutic target. This prediction was validated in silico via molecular docking and Boolean network modeling, and experimentally in a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and in a neuronal oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model. RESULTS: Network pharmacology and PPI analysis identified NOX4 as a central target, and molecular docking supported a stable interaction between C-3-G and NOX4. Transcriptomic profiling showed Nox4 upregulation with enrichment of oxidative-stress and cell-death pathways; Boolean network simulations indicated that inhibiting Nox4 attenuates the ROS-injury cascade. In experimental validation, C-3-G reduced infarct size and cerebral edema and improved neurological function in the MCAO mouse model, accompanied by decreased MDA, restoration of SOD and GSH activities, inhibition of Nox4 activity, and normalization of the Nrf2-Keap1-HO-1 axis toward homeostasis. The in vitro findings were concordant with the in vivo results. Co-administration of C-3-G with the Nox4-selective inhibitor GLX351322 produced no additive benefit, indicating that C-3-G exerts its neuroprotective effects predominantly via the Nox4 pathway.Crucially, the neuroprotective effects of C-3-G were not additive with a selective NOX4 inhibitor, confirming NOX4 as its primary molecular target. CONCLUSION: C-3-G mitigates ischemia-reperfusion-induced oxidative stress and tissue injury by targeting Nox4 and modulating the Nrf2-Keap1-HO-1 antioxidant axis, supporting its potential as an adjunct therapy in the acute phase of ischemic stroke.
abstract_zh: 背景：旨在通过网络药理学和转录组学方法，探讨膳食花青素矢车菊素-3-葡萄糖苷（C-3-G）在脑缺血再灌注损伤中的神经保护作用，并阐明其潜在分子机制。方法：我们采用网络药理学和转录组学方法，将NOX4确定为核心治疗靶点。该预测通过分子对接和布尔网络建模在计算机模拟中验证，并在小鼠大脑中动脉闭塞（MCAO）模型和神经元氧糖剥夺/复氧（OGD/R）模型中进行了实验验证。结果：网络药理学和PPI分析将NOX4确定为中心靶点，分子对接支持C-3-G与NOX4之间的稳定相互作用。转录组学分析显示Nox4上调，并富集氧化应激和细胞死亡通路；布尔网络模拟表明，抑制Nox4可减弱ROS损伤级联反应。在实验验证中，C-3-G在MCAO小鼠模型中减少了梗死面积和脑水肿，并改善了神经功能，同时伴随MDA降低、SOD和GSH活性恢复、Nox4活性抑制，以及Nrf2-Keap1-HO-1轴向稳态正常化。体外结果与体内结果一致。C-3-G与Nox4选择性抑制剂GLX351322联合给药未产生额外益处，表明C-3-G主要通过Nox4通路发挥其神经保护作用。关键的是，C-3-G的神经保护作用与选择性NOX4抑制剂不具有叠加性，证实NOX4是其主要分子靶点。结论：C-3-G通过靶向Nox4并调节Nrf2-Keap1-HO-1抗氧化轴，减轻缺血再灌注诱导的氧化应激和组织损伤，支持其作为缺血性卒中急性期辅助治疗的潜力。
